reference: Martin & Moyce 1952, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 244, 312 (doi:10.1098/rsta.1952.0006)

time_convention.correct: T_MM = t*sqrt(2*g/a), X = x_front/a  (M&M definition; a = initial column WIDTH, column is a wide x 2a tall)
evidence: Lethe official post-processing examples/multiphysics/dam-break/dam-break-2d.py: time_list = [x * ((2*g/L1)**0.5) for x in time_list]; x_list = [x / L1 for x in x_list]  (verbatim)
K&O / Trixi-family digitisation agrees with the Lethe x_exp/y_exp digitisation
time_convention.old_wrong: T_code = t*sqrt(g/a)  (used by bench_fs_2d.py, dam_break_sc/run.py, dam_break_3d_mm/run.py) -- a factor sqrt(2) too small
time_convention.secondary_axis: T_MM_geff = t*sqrt(2*g_eff/a) with g_eff = g*(1-rho_v/rho_l) = 0.9184*g (reported for completeness; primary axis uses the M&M g)

checkpoint_basis: linear interpolation of the Lethe table; T=2.96 is the last tabulated point (T=3 would require extrapolation, forbidden by the repo no-extrapolation standard)

convention_and_table_fix.double_error_retraction: the historical +50~82% errors were the product of a DOUBLE error: (i) the axis T=t*sqrt(g/a) was missing a factor sqrt(2); (ii) the reference table was wrong. Both are now fixed; the +50% claims are RETRACTED.

table_1.why_wrong: mapped M&M's T=3 value (2.7) onto T=2 and used an unsourced T=1 value

table_2.why_wrong: coarse digitisation, only meaningful on the old t*sqrt(g/a) axis

official_rerun_correct_convention.note: real runs, CPU, 2026-09-29; X = X_toe/a interpolated on the T_MM axis; errors against 1.326/2.360/3.670

accuracy_le_3pct_fine_grid.detail: a=80: T=1 +2.49% PASS; T=2 -9.72% FAIL; T=2.96 -19.09% FAIL -> 1 of 3 checkpoints

gap.summary: Under the CORRECT convention (T=t*sqrt(2g/a)) and the CORRECT Lethe table, the SCMP front is only within 3% at the earliest checkpoint (a=80, T=1: +2.49%); the error grows monotonically with T (-9.7% at T=2, -19.1% at T=2.96). NOT verified.
gap.root_cause: mid/late-time dynamics: the simulated column collapses too fast (residual height H~0.16 vs M&M ~0.5+), so insufficient potential energy is converted to front momentum -> the front is systematically too slow for T>=2. This is a constitutive / density-ratio gap (SC94 at G=5 gives rho_l/rho_v ~ 13 vs M&M water/air ~800).
gap.retraction: the previously reported +50~82% SCMP errors were double-counted (axis x sqrt2 AND wrong table) and are withdrawn; the true errors are +2.5% / -9.7% / -19.1% at a=80.

recommendation: keep B20 in benchmarks/pending/ (do NOT move to verified) -- accuracy fails at T=2 and T=2.96
the metric of record for this benchmark is now the T_MM = t*sqrt(2g/a) axis with the Lethe table (1.326/2.360/3.670)
next lever: late-time column collapse (residual height H) -- a density-ratio / constitutive change, or a hybrid two-phase route
the historical +50% claims are retracted; the honest summary is 'close at early time (+2.5% at T=1), diverging to -19% by T=2.96'

supporting.fs2d_convention_fix: benchmarks/bench_fs_2d.py REF_T/REF_Z + T_TARGETS + SQRT_GA corrected to the T=t*sqrt(2g/a) convention (old table kept as a comment)
